sources.title: Metropolitan Museum of Art: Assyria, 1365 to 609 BCE
sources.note: Middle and Neo-Assyrian historical overview. Do not follow its erroneous 612 date for the fall of Ashur: primary Babylonian Chronicle ABC3 places that event in 614. No library-founder claim derived here.

sources.title: Metropolitan Museum of Art: human-headed winged bull, 32.143.1
sources.note: Direct catalogue, ca.883 to 859BCE, Nimrud; description explicitly explains five legs and doorway protection.

sources.title: ORACC Nimrud: the Northwest Palace
sources.note: Full indexed original: royal quarters south, wells in AB/AJ/NN/80, kitchen ZZ with benches, bread oven and cooking vessels. Direct access failed.

sources.title: Ludovico Portuese: Bathing Rooms in First-Millennium Assyria
sources.note: KASKAL n.s.1(2024),169 to 186. Full PDF read; printed170 to 172, figures1 to 2 distinguish physical drains from reconstructed toilet fittings.

sources.title: University of Cambridge: Ziyaret Tepe, a mound with a story
sources.note: John MacGinnis and Charis Goodyear. Indexed original feature: finds, administrative tools and games. Objects are site assemblage, not one reconstructed household.

sources.title: University of Cambridge: archaeologists discover lost language
sources.note: 10May2012; full indexed original.144 names,59 legible; western Iranian origin and deportee identity are hypotheses, not secure identifications. Ignore erroneous western-Turkey wording in closing bullets; main text locates southeastern Turkey.

sources.title: ORACC Nimrud: Assyrian scholarly professions
sources.note: Indexed original section on eighth-century Kalhu and approximately30 bread/wine lists; regular ration versus special-occasion supplement is unresolved.

sources.title: ORACC RINAP: Sennacherib 226, Jerwan inscription
sources.note: Full indexed original Q004031; stone blocks, reign704 to 681BCE, line1 exact MAN ŠÚ MAN KUR aš-šur; lines1 to 9 canal/aqueduct. Query "Q004031" "Jerwan" reproduces entire edition. Original glyph rendering unavailable; public sample explicitly scholarly transliteration.

sources.title: British Museum: What was Ashurbanipal’s Library?
sources.note: Indexed original2020 to 2024 project findings: over30,000 tablets from Nineveh, ownership colophons distinguish collections; editing/copying and deliberate destruction. Not30,000 intact library books.

sources.title: ORACC Nimrud: Scholarly works
sources.note: Indexed original, lexical lists and mobile libraries sections. Lists teach spelling and Sumerian/Akkadian vocabulary; scribal training and scholarly reference overlap.

sources.title: British Museum: reconstructing a 2,500-year-old medical encyclopaedia
sources.note: Indexed original project description,2020 to 2023. Prescriptions contain symptoms, drugs, preparation/administration instructions, sometimes prognosis; rituals also present. No modern efficacy claim.

sources.title: Kreppner and Schmid: architecture and stratigraphy of the Red House at Dur-Katlimmu
sources.note: Florian Jannoscha Kreppner and Jochen Schmid,2013,BATSH11. Direct English/German repository abstracts: elite residence continued beyond612 until fire mid-sixth century; four Assyrian texts dated under NebuchadnezzarII.

sources.title: Babylonian Chronicle ABC 3: the fall of Nineveh
sources.note: Direct primary translation, BM21901; Nabopolassar years12/14/16/17: Ashur614, Nineveh612, Harran610, unsuccessful recapture609. Assur-uballit subsequently disappears from written record; no known death asserted.

batchIdentityNotes.finding: Indexed1500 to 500BCE; all three imported polygons repeat bbox40.7866 to 46.1111E,33.3240 to 37.8143N, grossly understating Neo-Assyrian imperial extent. Public overview explains both outline and chronology mismatch. Narrative focuses Middle/Neo phases without declaring1500 foundation or500 state end. Existing curated fell/successors untouched by override omission. Existing fell wording is less precise than new sourced ending, which does not assert a known death of Assur-uballit in609.
